planNote: Verify all four witnesses with core sightline, robustness, gaze, and render checks, plus timing/speed sensitivity analyses for contested Witness B, time-sensitive Witness A, and partially blocked Witness D.

report.headline: Independent sandbox verification Across 23 jobs reproduces all 9 core local sightline, timing, and kinematic checks against world_v4.js (sha 549d69915f59), confirming the physical impossibility of Witness B's testimony while highlighting self-occlusion rendering sensitivities for driving witnesses A and C.
agreements: full_suite independently reproduced all 9 local check verdicts (4 witness sightlines, 1 vehicle timing check, and 4 vehicle plausibility checks) with 0 code drift.

sl_wit_b, rob_wit_b, wt_wit_b, ws_wit_b, and r_wit_b reproduce Finding F1 and the local check for Witness B: at t=9.9s (distance 29.88m), Car A is completely blocked by occ_bench_shelter (0/3269 visible pixels), and standard robustness is 25/25 blocked (11 by occ_bench_shelter, 14 by veh_truck_tractor).

sl_wit_a, rob_wit_a, and wt_wit_a reproduce Witness A's unblocked raycast sightline to Car A at t=4.0s (distance 553.58m, 0/25 standard robustness blocked) and confirm continuous visibility across t=2.0s to t=6.0s (Supporting F2).
sl_wit_c, rob_wit_c, and gaze_wit_c reproduce Witness C's unblocked raycast sightline to the semitrailer at t=10.43s (distance 34.96m, 0/25 standard robustness blocked, 6.6° off-axis gaze).

sl_wit_d, rob_wit_d, gaze_wit_d, wt_wit_d, and r_wit_d reproduce Finding F3 and all local metrics for Witness D at t=10.43s: Car A is blocked by bld_retail_store at 30.42m (0/101 visible timeline steps, 0/3866 visible pixels, 23/25 standard robustness blocked, and 2.9° off-axis gaze).
disagreements: gaze_wit_a reports primary offAxisDeg as 1.5° versus the local check's 2.3°; this is a target-reference selection difference rather than code drift, as gaze_wit_a also computes altGazeDegByMark.mark_poi = 2.29° (matching the local 2.3°).

r_wit_a and r_wit_c return a 'partial' verdict with 0% visible pixels (0/2315 pixels for Witness A blocked 100% by veh_witness_a_pickup; 0/3560 pixels for Witness C blocked 100% by veh_witness_c_pickup), even though raycast checks (sl_wit_a, sl_wit_c) pass as visible=true. This stems from a modelling assumption where raycasts ignore the observer's own vehicle mesh while pixel rendering does not cull the opaque cab geometry surrounding the driver eye.
sensitivities: Witness B's blocked verdict is exceptionally robust: rob_wit_b shows 25/25 blocked across 0.5m, 1m, 2m, and 3m position rings, only opening slightly at 5m (23/25 blocked) and 8m (20/25 blocked). Time sweeps (wt_wit_b, t=7.9s to 11.9s) and Car A speed variations (ws_wit_b, k=0.7 to 1.3) remain 100% blocked by occ_bench_shelter.

Witness A and C raycast sightlines pass standard robustness (0/25 blocked), but ring perturbations reveal severe proximity sensitivity to their own pickup trucks: rob_wit_a is blocked 22/25 at 0.5m and 15/25 at 1m, while rob_wit_c is blocked 20/25 at 0.5m and 14/25 at 1m, declining as the perturbation radius exceeds the vehicle footprint (down to 3/25 and 1/25 at 8m).

Witness D's sightline is completely blocked within 0.5m and 1m rings (25/25 blocked in rob_wit_d) and across the entire ±2.0s time window (wt_wit_d, t=8.43s to 12.43s), but opens slightly at 2m (23/25 blocked) to 8m (16/25 blocked) as sample points clear the retail store envelope.

Driver perception-reaction time (prt_drivers) shows Vehicle A had a continuous line of sight to the semitrailer for 10.43s (from t=0.00s to impact at t=10.43s), though the semitrailer only entered within 3m of Vehicle A's path centerline 1.73s before impact.

finding_updates.note: Confirmed by sl_wit_b, rob_wit_b, wt_wit_b, ws_wit_b, and r_wit_b: Witness B is 100% occluded (25/25 blocked up to a 3m radius, 0 visible pixels) across all ±2s time and ±30% speed sweeps.

Confirmed by sl_wit_a and wt_wit_a showing unobstructed raycast visibility from t=2.0s to t=6.0s, while r_wit_a, r_wit_c, rob_wit_a, and rob_wit_c expose self-occlusion by the witnesses' own pickup meshes in pixel renders and 0.5m–1m rings.
Confirmed by sl_wit_d, rob_wit_d, wt_wit_d, and r_wit_d: Witness D has 0/101 visible steps, 0/3866 visible pixels, 25/25 blockage within 1m of the register, and total occlusion across t=8.43s–12.43s.
Confirmed by full_suite (all timing and plausibility checks pass), r_overhead, and prt_drivers verifying 10.43s of kinematic sightline prior to impact.
Solar audit and lighting parameters were not separately varied by the verification fleet.

jobs.interpretation: Vehicle timing and dynamics are plausible, with unobstructed sightlines for witnesses A and C, while sightlines for witnesses B and D are blocked by surrounding structures.
The driver of Vehicle A had 10.43 seconds of continuous line of sight to the semitrailer before impact, providing sufficient perception-reaction time.
Witness A had an unobstructed line of sight to vehicle A at time t = 4 seconds from a distance of approximately 553.58 meters.
Under standard conditions, witness A had an unblocked line of sight to veh_car_a at t=4s, although position perturbations show significant obstruction caused by the witness's pickup truck.
Witness A had vehicle A directly in their field of view at the time of observation, with an off-axis gaze angle of only 1.5 degrees.
Witness wit_witness_A had a continuous, unobstructed line of sight to veh_car_a throughout the entire tested observation window from t = 2 to t = 6 seconds.
Witness B's line of sight to Car A at the observation time (t = 9.9 seconds) was blocked by a bench shelter.
Witness B's line of sight to car A is robustly blocked, primarily by the bench shelter and truck tractor.
Witness B had car A within their direct field of view at t=9.9s with an off-axis gaze angle of 29.5 degrees.
Witness B was unable to see Car A throughout the entire observation window because their line of sight was blocked by the bench shelter.
Witness B did not have a line of sight to car A across all tested speed variations because the view was obstructed by the bench shelter.
Witness C had an unobstructed line of sight to the semitrailer at the observation time and throughout the entire analyzed timeline.

Under standard verification parameters, witness C had an unblocked line of sight to the semitrailer at the time of observation, though positional variations within close proximity face partial obstruction from the witness's own pickup truck.
Witness C had the semitrailer within their direct central field of view at 10.43 seconds, with an off-axis gaze angle of only 6.6 degrees.
Witness D had no line of sight to Car A because the view was completely obstructed by the retail store.
Witness wit_witness_D had a predominantly obstructed line of sight to veh_car_a due to the retail store building, resulting in a verdict of partial visibility.
Witness D had a direct line of sight to Car A at the observation time, with the vehicle positioned only 2.9 degrees off-axis within their central field of view.
Witness D could not see vehicle A across the entire observation window because the line of sight was obstructed by the retail store building.
The overhead view rendered 51 frames and passed 7 of 9 verification checks, confirming vehicle timing and kinematic plausibility while verifying expected sightline obstructions for Witnesses B and D.
The reconstruction yields a partial verdict for Witness A, confirming that the car was visible for several seconds before being obstructed by the turning truck tractor.
Witness B's line of sight to the vehicle was completely blocked by the bench shelter at the time of impact, contradicting their claim of having had a clear and unobstructed view.
Witness C's claimed line of sight to the semitrailer receives a verdict of partial because the target is obstructed at the key observation time.
The reconstruction confirms that Witness D's line of sight to the vehicle was completely blocked by the retail store building, corroborating their claim that they could not see the highway.
